REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City SERVICE BWAHENC P'NOY WZAtm.AD' HON. LILAND ZOILA B. ESTACION, M.D. HON. JESSICA JANE VILLANUEVA-KOPPIN HON. GEORGITA F. MARTINEZ Sangguniang Panlalawigan Members 1st District, Negros Oriental Ladies: Legal Opinion No. 34 s. 2011 JUL 11 2011 AND LOGA'. e E LEA s ED NO. This has reference to your letter dated 08 July 2011 requesting this Department's legal opinion on the holding of chairmanship in the outstanding committees by ex-officio members in the Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP). Per your letter, you were recently removed from the chairmanship of outstanding committees in the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in favor of ex-officio members. Hence, your are now planning to lodge a protest in order not to deprive the minority and your constituents of the proper representation in your province's local sanggunian. At the outset, please be inforrned that the matter of deciding whether or not to reorganize the various committees in the sanggunian or even as to how many times it may reorganize is the sole prerogative of the legislative body. Coming now to your query, please be informed that the Provincial Councilor's League (PCL) President, Liga ng mga Barangay Provincial Chapter (LBPC) President and SK Provincial Federation (SKPF) President acquired their right to sit as ex-officio members of the SP by reason of their having been elected as President of their respective league or federation, whose election thereto also arose originally from their having been elected as Sangguniang Bayan/ Panlungsod Member, Punong Barangay and SK Chairman, within their respective locality. May we note that the Punong Barangay and SK Chairman are by nature non- partisan local officials. Their non-partisan nature is not obliterated the moment they are elected as President of their respective Liga or Federation and sit as ex-officio members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. This non-partisan character also applies to PCL President since the same assumed the ex-officio membership in the SP in representation, not of his political party (if he belongs to any), but of the federation. Being non-partisan, as a general rule, they should not be considered in the determination of the majority and minority parties in the sanggunian when it comes to the organization/re-organization of the standing committees. This Department has been consistent in its opinion that, as a general rule, ex-officio members of the sanggunian are not allowed to participate and vote in the committee reorganization because the same is based on political party affiliation. Anyway, ex-officio members of the sanggunian are assured of their respective committee chairmanship prescribed under the law. For example, the LBPC President shall automatically hold the chairmanship of the Committee on Barangay Affairs (Art. 108 [b] [I] of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the Local Government Code).

2- However, there is an exception to this general rule, that is, if the SP"s duly approved Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP) expressly allows the ex-officio members to do so. Hence, if your IRP allows ex-officio members to become members of the standing committees that may otherwise be created by the SP, then this provision shall prevail. On the contrary, if your IRP limits the membership of ex-officio members to those allowed under the law, this provision prevails. If your sanggunian IRP failed to address the issue, the chairman and members for each committee shall be elected from among its regular members applying the general rule discussed above. We hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, SUS . DOQUE IV ector III Ls/17 Copy furnished: RD PEDRO A. NOVAL, CESO 111 DILG Region VII Sudlon, Lahug, Cebu City PROVINCIAL DIRECTOR DILG-Negros Oriental
